units.t: Measurement and Motion in One Dimension

learn: Physics uses SI units: metres, kilograms, seconds, amperes, kelvin.
Significant figures show measurement precision.
Dimensional analysis checks equations and converts units.
check: The SI unit of mass is the...
lessons.try: Convert 72 km/h to m/s.

learn: Displacement is change in position (a vector); distance is total path (a scalar).
Velocity = displacement/time; acceleration = change in velocity/time.
Position-time graph slope gives velocity; velocity-time slope gives acceleration.
check: A car going from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s accelerates at...
Area under a velocity-time graph gives...
lessons.try: Draw position-time and velocity-time graphs for a walk.

learn: v = v₀ + at; x = v₀t + ½at²; v² = v₀² + 2ax.
Near Earth, free-fall acceleration g is about 9.8 m/s² downward.
Ignoring air resistance, all objects fall at the same rate.
check: A stone dropped falls ___ in 3 s (g = 9.8).
After 2 s of free fall from rest, v is...
Without air resistance, heavy and light objects fall...
lessons.try: Calculate how far a stone falls in 3 seconds.

learn: Vectors have magnitude and direction; add them tip to tail.
Components: x = A cos θ, y = A sin θ.
Magnitude from components: √(x² + y²).
check: 3 m east plus 4 m north has magnitude...
A 10 N force at 30° has x-component...
lessons.try: Add a 3 m east and 4 m north displacement.

learn: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent.
Horizontal velocity stays constant (no air resistance); vertical velocity changes by g.
A ball dropped and one thrown sideways from the same height land together.
check: Horizontal velocity of a projectile is...
A dropped and a thrown ball land...
Vertical acceleration of a projectile is...
lessons.try: Predict where a ball rolled off a table will land.

learn: On level ground, maximum range occurs at 45° (no air resistance).
Complementary angles (30° and 60°) give the same range.
Time of flight depends on vertical velocity.
check: Maximum range on level ground is at...
Time of flight depends on ___ velocity.
lessons.try: Use a simulation (PhET Projectile Motion) to test launch angles.

learn: An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a net force acts.
Inertia depends on mass.
Seat belts protect passengers from their own inertia.
lessons.try: Explain the tablecloth trick with inertia.

learn: F_net = ma; force in newtons (kg·m/s²).
Free-body diagrams show all forces on an object.
Weight = mg.
check: A 5 kg object with 20 N net force accelerates at...
lessons.try: Draw a free-body diagram for a book on a table.

lessons.t: Third Law, Friction and Normal Force
learn: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction on a different object.
Friction opposes motion; f = μN.
Normal force is perpendicular to the surface.
check: With μ = 0.3 and N = 100 N, friction is...
Normal force is ___ to the surface.
lessons.try: Measure friction coefficients with a spring scale.

learn: Objects in circular motion accelerate toward the centre (centripetal).
a = v²/r; F = mv²/r.
Without centripetal force, objects move in a straight line (tangent).
check: v = 10 m/s, r = 5 m gives a =
lessons.try: Swing a soft ball on a string and observe what happens when it is released.

learn: F = Gm₁m₂/r²; G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².
Gravity follows an inverse-square law.
Doubling distance makes gravity a quarter as strong.
check: Newton's law of gravitation applies to...
lessons.try: Calculate the force between Earth and the Moon.

learn: Kepler: orbits are ellipses; equal areas in equal times; T² is proportional to r³.
Satellites are in continuous free fall around Earth.
Astronauts feel weightless because they fall with their spacecraft.
check: Kepler's third law relates period and...
lessons.try: Explain why the ISS doesn't fall to Earth.

learn: W = Fd cos θ; measured in joules.
No work is done if there is no displacement or the force is perpendicular.
Work transfers energy.
check: Carrying a box horizontally at constant speed does ___ work against gravity.
lessons.try: Calculate the work to lift a 2 kg book 1.5 m.

learn: KE = ½mv²; gravitational PE = mgh; elastic PE = ½kx².
Energy is conserved in a closed system.
Roller coasters trade PE and KE.
check: A 2 kg ball at 3 m/s has KE...
Speed after a 20 m drop (no friction) is about...
lessons.try: Predict a roller coaster's speed at the bottom of a 20 m drop.

learn: Power = work/time, measured in watts.
Efficiency = useful output/input × 100%.
Friction turns some energy into heat.
check: 80 J useful from 100 J input is ___ efficient.
lessons.try: Measure your power climbing stairs.

learn: Momentum p = mv; impulse = FΔt = Δp.
Increasing collision time reduces force (airbags, crumple zones).
Momentum is a vector.
check: A 1,000 kg car at 20 m/s has momentum...
lessons.try: Explain how an airbag works using impulse.

learn: In a closed system, total momentum before equals total momentum after.
Recoil: a launcher moves back when a ball is launched forward.
Rockets push exhaust backward to move forward.
check: Total momentum in a closed system is...
A 2 kg cart at 3 m/s hits a still 1 kg cart and they stick; their speed is...
lessons.try: Use carts to demonstrate momentum conservation.

learn: Elastic: kinetic energy conserved. Inelastic: some KE lost.
Perfectly inelastic: objects stick together.
Momentum is conserved in both.
check: Kinetic energy is conserved in ___ collisions.
lessons.try: Compare bouncing and sticking collisions.

learn: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.
v = fλ; frequency in hertz.
Transverse waves vibrate perpendicular; longitudinal waves parallel.
check: A wave at 5 Hz with λ = 2 m has speed...
lessons.try: Make waves on a slinky and identify each type.

learn: Sound travels about 343 m/s in air at 20 °C, faster in liquids and solids.
Pitch depends on frequency; loudness on amplitude (measured in decibels).
The Doppler effect: pitch rises as a source approaches.
check: Thunder 3 s after lightning is about ___ away.
lessons.try: Estimate a lightning strike's distance from the thunder delay.

learn: Constructive interference adds waves; destructive cancels them.
Standing waves form at specific frequencies in strings and pipes.
Resonance occurs when a driving frequency matches a natural frequency.
lessons.try: Explore standing waves with the PhET Wave on a String simulation.

learn: Light is an electromagnetic wave travelling at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
The spectrum runs from radio to gamma rays; visible light is a small part.
Light also behaves as particles (photons).
check: The speed of light is about...
The highest frequency EM wave is...
lessons.try: Rank EM waves by frequency.

learn: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Plane mirrors make virtual, upright images.
Concave mirrors can focus light; convex mirrors widen the view.
check: Angle of incidence equals the angle of...
lessons.try: Use a ray diagram to locate an image in a concave mirror.

learn: Light bends when changing speed between media; Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.
Converging (convex) lenses focus light; diverging (concave) spread it.
Lens equation: 1/f = 1/dₒ + 1/dᵢ.
check: An object 30 cm from a 10 cm lens has an image at...
Light bending at a boundary is...
lessons.try: Find the image distance for an object 30 cm from a 10 cm lens.

learn: Charge is measured in coulombs; like charges repel.
Current is the flow of charge (amperes); voltage is energy per charge (volts).
Coulomb's law: F = kq₁q₂/r².
lessons.try: Explain static electricity with a balloon.

learn: V = IR; resistance in ohms.
Electrical power P = IV = I²R.
Energy used = power × time (kWh on bills).
lessons.try: Calculate the monthly cost of running a device.

learn: Series: one path, resistances add, same current.
Parallel: multiple paths, same voltage, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
Homes use parallel circuits so devices work independently; fuses and breakers protect them.
check: 4 Ω and 6 Ω in series total...
6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel total...
lessons.try: Build series and parallel circuits in the PhET Circuit Construction Kit.

learn: Magnets have north and south poles; field lines run north to south outside.
Moving charges create magnetic fields; electromagnets use coils.
Earth's magnetic field protects us from solar wind.
check: Field lines run ___ outside a magnet.
lessons.try: Map a magnet's field with a compass.

learn: Changing magnetic fields induce currents (Faraday, 1831).
Generators turn motion into electricity; motors turn electricity into motion.
Transformers change voltage for power transmission.
lessons.try: Make a simple generator by moving a magnet through a coil.

learn: Einstein's relativity: nothing travels faster than light; E = mc².
Quantum physics: energy comes in packets; the photoelectric effect.
Nuclear physics: fission and fusion release energy; the Sun runs on fusion.
lessons.try: Research how one modern technology depends on quantum physics.
